title: 14 charged in deadly train-container smuggling scheme that killed 7, including a child
excerpt: A federal grand jury has charged 14 people in a human smuggling operation that left seven people dead inside a sealed shipping container on a train bound for Laredo, the Justice Department announced Monday.
content:
A federal grand jury in the Western District of Texas has returned a superseding indictment charging 14 people in a human smuggling operation that left seven people dead inside a sealed shipping container on a train bound for Laredo, the U.S. Department of Justice announced Monday.

According to the Justice Department, the defendants include seven people in the country illegally, three other non-citizens and four U.S. citizens. Prosecutors say the group operated a smuggling organization from at least April 2023 through May 12, 2026, moving people across the southern border from Mexico and then loading them into shipping containers on cargo trains to carry them farther into the United States. Each person smuggled, or their family, paid between $1,500 and $10,000, according to court documents cited by the department.

The deadly event at the center of the case began in February 2026, when the organization began arranging the smuggling of at least seven people, including a 14-year-old child from Honduras, into Del Rio. On or about May 9, after the group was crossed into the Del Rio area, smugglers took them to an area near the Union Pacific train tracks and, between about 1:18 p.m. and 1:25 p.m., used red bolt cutters to cut the lock off a Conex shipping container on a stationary train, loaded the seven people inside and shut the door, according to the Justice Department.

The container was stacked on top of another, had no ventilation or cooling system, was secured from the outside and could not be opened from the inside, the department said. Outside temperatures that day ranged from 88 to 92 degrees. The train traveled east along U.S. Highway 90 to San Antonio, where smugglers opened the container, found the people inside in peril and fled, allegedly leaving one person who had died near the railroad tracks. The remaining victims were left in the container, and the train continued south to Laredo the next day.

On May 10, a worker at the Union Pacific Rail Yard in Laredo saw a leg sticking out of a Conex shipping container. Inside, six people were found dead. San Antonio law enforcement later found the seventh victim dead and abandoned by the railroad tracks in San Antonio. Four of the dead were Mexican nationals and three were Honduran nationals, including the 14-year-old child. Investigators found that at least one victim had messaged a loved one pleading for help.

Eleven of the defendants were indicted in July. The superseding indictment charges 12 defendants with conspiracy to transport people resulting in death and aiding and abetting transportation resulting in death, which carry a maximum penalty of life in prison if convicted. Eleven defendants are also charged with conspiracy to commit money laundering, carrying a maximum of 20 years.

"Seven people are dead as the result of another callous alien smuggling scheme," U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons for the Western District of Texas said in the department's announcement.

The case was investigated by Homeland Security Investigations offices in Del Rio, Laredo, San Antonio, Houston, Dallas and El Paso, U.S. Border Patrol and other agencies, with assistance from the Laredo Police Department, the Texas Department of Public Safety and Union Pacific Railroad Police, among others.

An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

Sources: U.S. Department of Justice, November 9, 2026; U.S. Attorney's Office for the Western District of Texas.
